title: High-fidelity geometric quantum gates exceeding 99.9% in germanium quantum dots
authors: Yu-Chen Zhou, Rong-Long Ma, Zhenzhen Kong, Ao-Ran Li, Chengxian Zhang, Xin Zhang, Yang Liu, Hao-Tian Jiang, Zhi-Tao Wu, Gui-Lei Wang, Gang Cao, Guang-Can Guo, Hai-Ou Li, Guo-Ping Guo
abstract: Achieving high-fidelity and robust qubit manipulations is a crucial requirement for realizing faulttolerant quantum computation. Here, we demonstrate a single-hole spin qubit in a germanium quantum dot and characterize its control fidelity using gate set tomography. The maximum control fidelities reach 97.48%, 99.81%, 99.88% for the I, X/2 and Y /2 gate, respectively. These results reveal that off-resonance noise during consecutive I gates in gate set tomography sequences severely limits qubit performance. Therefore, we introduce geometric quantum computation to realize noiseresilient qubit manipulation. The geometric gate control fidelities remain above 99% across a wide range of Rabi frequencies. The maximum fidelity surpasses 99.9%. Furthermore, the fidelities of geometric X/2 and Y /2 (I) gates exceed 99% even when detuning the microwave frequency by +-2.5 MHz (+-1.2 MHz), highlighting the noise-resilient feature. These results demonstrate that geometric quantum computation is a potential method for achieving high-fidelity qubit manipulation reproducibly in semiconductor quantum computation.
summary: This work reports on achieving high-fidelity quantum gate operations using a single-hole spin qubit in a germanium quantum dot. By implementing geometric quantum computation, the researchers overcame fidelity limitations caused by off-resonance noise inherent in standard gate sequences. This demonstrates a promising, robust pathway toward scalable quantum computation in solid-state semiconductor platforms.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving high-fidelity and robust qubit manipulations necessary for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that implementing geometric quantum computation allows for qubit gate fidelities exceeding 99.9%, significantly outperforming standard dynamical gate methods, especially under noise conditions.
method: The research involves characterizing single-qubit gate control fidelities using gate set tomography (GST) and comparing these results against those obtained using geometric quantum computation (GQC) protocols.
model_or_system: The platform utilized is a single-hole spin qubit housed within a germanium quantum dot, controlled via Electric Dipole Spin Resonance (EDSR) mediated by intrinsic spin-orbit interaction (SOI).
key_observables: Control fidelities for I, X/2, and Y/2 gates; Rabi frequency ($\omega_{Rabi}$); dephasing time ($T_2^*$).
important_parameters: Gate fidelities exceeding 99.9%; microwave frequency detuning ($\pm 2.5$ MHz); Rabi frequency range up to 19 MHz.
main_assumptions: Standard gate sequences are severely limited by off-resonance noise, which GQC is proposed to overcome.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure (SEM, cross-section), qubit characterization (Rabi/CPMG decay), and critically, compare the fidelity of dynamical gates versus geometric gates under varying Rabi frequencies and detunings.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical system and the need for high fidelity. It then characterizes the qubit using standard methods (GST) to identify noise limitations. The core contribution is the introduction and demonstration of GQC, showing its superior, noise-resilient performance compared to the standard methods.
why_interesting: The focus on geometric control is highly relevant to open quantum systems, as it provides a mechanism to engineer robustness against environmental noise (like detuning) by leveraging geometric phases, a concept applicable across many physical platforms.
